record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For k-CLIQUE, where k is fixed and the input is an undirected simple loopless p-vertex graph G and the task is to decide whether G contains a clique on k vertices, design algorithms with better time complexity, better space complexity, or both, than the available fixed-k clique algorithms.

evidence.quote: Design algorithms with better time and/or space complexities for k-CLIQUE!

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer k ≥ 3. The k-CLIQUE problem is defined as follows: given an undirected simple loopless graph G on p vertices, decide whether G contains a clique on k vertices (i.e., a subset of k pairwise adjacent vertices).

The currently fastest known algorithms for k-CLIQUE (with fixed k) reduce the problem to fast matrix multiplication, yielding a running time of O(p^{ωk/3}) (where ω < 2.373 is the matrix-multiplication exponent), due to Nešetřil and Poljak. The space complexity of such algorithms is polynomial in p.

Problem: Design an algorithm for k-CLIQUE that achieves either
(a) asymptotically better worst-case time complexity than O(p^{ωk/3}), or
(b) asymptotically better worst-case space complexity than the existing matrix-multiplication-based methods while keeping competitive time, or
(c) simultaneous improvement in both time and space complexity,
where the bounds are measured as functions of p with k held fixed.
artifact.status_search_result: The Nešetřil–Poljak algorithm (1985) running in O(n^{ωk/3}) time remains the asymptotically fastest known algorithm for detecting a k-clique with fixed k. Despite considerable effort, no improvement to this exponent is known in general; only minor improvements for specific residues of k modulo 3 and small k have been reported. The problem of improving its time and/or space complexity remains open.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Algorithms for Clique Problems (Vassilevska)
status_evidence.snippet: When k is a fixed constant, the asymptotically fastest known algorithm for finding a k-clique runs in O(n^{ωk/3}) time, due to Nešetřil and Poljak.
status_evidence.claim: The Nešetřil–Poljak bound remains the best known for fixed-k clique detection.

status_evidence.title: Graph Pattern Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements over the fastest known methods for k ≡ 1 (mod 3), k ≤ 16, and k ≡ 2 (mod 3), k > 5.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial improvements over Nešetřil–Poljak are known for specific cases.
